claims: The 2027 Social Security cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) is projected to be around 2.8% based on early 2026 data.
The 2027 Social Security COLA projection of 2.8% would match the 2026 increase.
A 2.8% increase would bring an average retired worker's monthly benefit up from $2,024.77 to $2,081.46.
Estimates for the 2027 Social Security COLA range up to 3.2% due to energy price volatility.
Key 2027 COLA forecast details are as of April 2026.
Analyst Mary Johnson estimates up to 3.2% for the 2027 COLA based on rising oil and energy costs.
A 2.8% raise would provide approximately $56.69 more per month for the average retiree.
Key drivers of the 2027 COLA forecast include inflation data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, particularly in food and medical care.
57.6% of seniors report having to skip medical services to cut costs.
The official 2027 COLA percentage will not be finalized until mid-October 2026.
The official 2027 COLA percentage is based on inflation data for the third quarter (July, August, September) of 2026.
Some proposals suggest utilizing the Consumer Price Index for the Elderly (CPI-E) to calculate the COLA.
